# Template: periodic_table
The periodic table, from real data for all 118 elements: the whole 18-column table; a SUBSET (`group`, `period`, `category`, `first` or a named list) drawn large with names; or one element as a detail card with its mass and electron configuration. `colour_by` washes the cells by a property, which is how periodicity becomes visible. Every cell is its own id (`cell_Fe`), so any element can be drawn, highlighted or pointed at by name. Choose this for ANY request about the periodic table, a group or period of elements, periodic trends, metals vs non-metals, noble gases, halogens, alkali metals, electron configuration, atomic number, or where an element sits among the others.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "element": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "ONE element as a big detail card. Accepts a symbol, an atomic number, or a name in English, Norwegian or Latin — \"Fe\", \"26\", \"iron\", \"jern\", \"ferrum\" all mean iron."
  },
  "elements": {
   "type": "array",
   "maxItems": 30,
   "items": {
    "type": "string"
   },
   "description": "Elements to draw, in their real table positions, e.g. [\"Na\", \"Cl\"]. Same spellings as `element`."
  },
  "group": {
   "type": "integer",
   "minimum": 1,
   "maximum": 18,
   "description": "One group (column): 1 alkali metals, 17 halogens, 18 noble gases."
  },
  "period": {
   "type": "integer",
   "minimum": 1,
   "maximum": 7,
   "description": "One period (row)."
  },
  "first": {
   "type": "integer",
   "minimum": 2,
   "maximum": 118,
   "description": "Only the first N by atomic number — \"the first 20\" is a standard school table."
  },
  "category": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "alkali-metal",
    "alkaline-earth-metal",
    "transition-metal",
    "post-transition-metal",
    "metalloid",
    "nonmetal",
    "halogen",
    "noble-gas",
    "lanthanide",
    "actinide"
   ],
   "description": "Only one category."
  },
  "colour_by": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "none",
    "category",
    "electronegativity",
    "radius",
    "state",
    "discovered",
    "block"
   ],
   "description": "Wash the cells by a property (default none). No measured value = blank cell."
  },
  "names": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "en",
    "nb",
    "la"
   ],
   "description": "Name language: en (default), nb, or la (the Latin that explains the symbol: Fe ferrum, Na natrium). Match the request's language."
  },
  "highlight": {
   "type": "array",
   "maxItems": 12,
   "items": {
    "type": "string"
   },
   "description": "Elements to mark, e.g. [\"F\", \"Cl\"] — each gets id highlight_<i>, revealable one at a time."
  },
  "legend": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Colour key under the table (default true when colour_by is set)."
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- grid: the frame plus the group numbers on top and the period numbers down the left (a group)
- cell_<Sym>: one element's cell — box, atomic number, symbol, and name/mass when drawn large. `cell_Fe`, `cell_H`. Draw, highlight, point at or zoom into these.
- fill_<Sym>: that cell's colour wash (colour_by only) — its own id, so the table can be drawn plain and coloured in afterwards
- highlight_<i>: the mark on highlight[i]
- legend: the colour key, when drawn
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Show the periodic table, coloured by category." → params: {"colour_by":"category","title":"The periodic table"}
Request: "Show me the halogens." → params: {"group":17,"colour_by":"category","title":"Group 17: the halogens"}
Request: "Hvorfor heter jern Fe?" → params: {"element":"Fe","names":"la"}

In YAML: `template: periodic_table` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
